brief: This Goldman Sachs daily monitor reports several unconnected items rather than arguing one thesis. US September nonfarm payrolls printed +29k, well below estimates, with the unemployment rate ticking up to 4.2% and the prior two months revised downward. France proposed that European countries and IEA members jointly release strategic reserves: 50 million barrels of diesel from European countries and 50 million barrels of crude from IEA members. The OAT-Bund spread broke through 130bps with spillover into BTPs; the note attributes this to structural challenges on rising French debt concerns and upcoming French elections creating a political risk premium, alongside a notable shift in EURUSD skew. Separately, Korea's Finance Minister said treasury bond issuance could be cut further if needed. Thai exports are getting an AI-demand boost despite 70% import-dependent inputs. Romania's central bank let the RON weaken 1.7% against the EUR. The IMF confirmed Senegalese authorities have met with bilateral creditors.
